An English crib of the Latin text, semi-literal, made for this database in 2026 with Claude, a large language model (LLM) made by Anthropic. It keeps close to the wording of the original and uses the established English of Anglo-Latin legal, liturgical and canon-law formulae. It is an aid to reading the original, not a published translation. Square brackets mark Liebermann’s additions to the text or, now and then, words supplied for the sense; “[?]” marks a doubtful reading

div.head: ECf 13.1 A 3
div.ab: Temporibus uero regum Danorum sepultum fuit ius in regno, leges et consuetudines simul sopite; temporibusque illorum praua uoluntas et uis et uiolentia magis regnabant quam iudicium in terra.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 640 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 13, 1, and numbers 13, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 13, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

seg.hi: fortlaufende Abschrift beendet hiermit und trägt fernere Stücke am unteren Rande ein Ce

note.seg: Ce ends its continuous copy here and enters further pieces in the lower margin

div.ab: But in the times of the kings of the Danes right was buried in the kingdom, laws and customs alike lulled to sleep; and in their times wicked will and force and violence reigned more than judgment in the land.
